cards.text: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church in Philippi, and he's in chains while he writes it (Philippians 1:13). He's near the end of his letter, and now he gets to the thank-you part. He says he rejoices greatly in the Lord that at last they've revived their concern for him.

cards.question: Paul says the Philippians cared about him all along. So why hadn't they shown it?

answers.text: They had no opportunity to show it
They didn't know where he was staying
They were waiting for him to ask them

cards.text: Then Paul jumps in quick: he's not saying this out of need. Not like me when a baker brings me cookies, going "Oh, you didn't have to!" while my mustache is ALREADY halfway in the box.

cards.question: Paul says he has learned to be ___ regardless of his circumstances.

cards.text: Paul says he knows how to live humbly, and he knows how to abound. In any and every situation, he's learned a secret.

cards.question: Paul says the secret he's learned, in any and every situation, is how to always have plenty.

cards.text: And then Paul says the line people put on everything from T-shirts to gym walls.

cards.question: Paul says he can do all things. Through whom?

answers.text: Through Christ who gives him strength
Through the friends who support him
Through Timothy who serves with him

cards.text: But Paul doesn't want the Philippians thinking their help didn't matter. He tells them they did well.

cards.question: Paul tells the Philippians they have done well to share in his ___.

cards.text: Then Paul takes them back to the early days of the gospel, when he left Macedonia, the region Philippi is in (Acts 16:12). He's going through the old receipts, and friend, I KNOW receipts, because I spent years under a pile of them in a junk drawer.

cards.question: When Paul left Macedonia, how many churches besides the Philippians partnered with him in giving and receiving?
Paul says even while he was in Thessalonica, the Philippians provided for his needs. How often?

cards.text: Then Paul tells them what he's really looking for when they give.

cards.question: Paul tells the Philippians he's seeking a gift from them, not the fruit that may be credited to their account.

cards.text: Their gifts reached Paul by Epaphroditus, the messenger the Philippians sent to take care of his needs (Philippians 2:25). Special delivery to a man in chains, no tracking number, just faith and a good pair of sandals.

cards.question: After getting the gifts from Epaphroditus, Paul says he has all he needs and more.
Paul says the Philippians' gifts are well-pleasing to God. What does he call them?

cards.text: Then Paul tells them his God will supply all their needs. Not most. Not just the big ones. ALL.

cards.question: Paul says God will supply all the Philippians' needs. According to what?

answers.text: His glorious riches in Christ Jesus
How much they have given to Paul

cards.text: Paul bursts into praise: "To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen."
Then he tells them, "Greet all the saints in Christ Jesus." The brothers with Paul send greetings, and so do all the saints.

cards.question: All the saints with Paul send greetings to the Philippians. Which saints does Paul point out especially?

answers.text: Those from the church in Jerusalem
Those from the city of Ephesus

cards.text: Saints in the household of Caesar, the Roman emperor himself, sending greetings all the way to Philippi! Then Paul signs off: "The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit."
